ko.executive_summary: SK Hynix launching aggressive AI-era talent acquisition campaign with restructured recruitment (removing educational requirements, streamlining to half-day interviews) while intensifying HBM competition with Samsung across product, investment, and hiring. Power architecture emerges as critical infrastructure bottleneck for scaling AI compute, and UBS reports Nvidia adjusted Rubin Ultra HBM specifications while demand and pricing remain elevated.
key_facts: SK Hynix eliminating educational background requirements in first college recruitment
SK Hynix conducting half-day in-depth interviews instead of traditional written applications
Samsung and SK Hynix engaged in full-scale HBM competition (product, investment, hiring)
Nvidia controls 60% of advanced packaging queue
Anthropic hired Microsoft veteran Eric Boyd for infrastructure capabilities
OpenAI ramping up Apple talent hiring (Jony Ive hardware initiative)

implications.text: SK Hynix and Samsung competing intensely for semiconductor talent; SK Hynix modernizing recruitment to attract AI-era engineers, creating spillover pressure on other Korean conglomerates
Full-front competition across product roadmap, capex allocation, and human capital signals critical importance of HBM for AI infrastructure dominance
Power architecture (not just wattage) becoming constraint for accelerated computing scale; infrastructure vendors gaining strategic leverage
Nvidia's 60% control of advanced packaging queue indicates sustained supply leverage and potential margin defense

ko.counterpoint: Nvidia HBM adjustments may reflect yield optimization rather than demand weakness.

ko.executive_summary: Microsoft accelerating in-house AI chip strategy with Maia 300 launching September, targeting 300,000 units from TSMC in 2024 and 1M+ total units, while competing against Nvidia's dominant position. Taiwan fabless designers advancing AI projects toward mass production; Alchip achieved record 3nm AI chip production in July with revenue doubling to NT$7.4B. Korean chipmakers' aggressive hiring (Samsung, SK Hynix) draining fabless talent pool and stressing local design ecosystem.
key_facts: Microsoft Maia 300 launching September 2024
Microsoft seeking 300,000 TSMC units for 2024; 1M+ total Maia 300 units planned
Nvidia controls 60% of advanced packaging queue
Alchip July revenue NT$7.4 billion (doubled), record 3nm AI chip production
Taiwan chip designers moving AI projects to mass production
Samsung, SK Hynix hiring draining Korean fabless talent

implications.text: Microsoft, Google, AWS competing via custom silicon; reducing reliance on Nvidia and reshaping AI chip market dynamics
300K+ units for Microsoft Maia 300 competes with Nvidia demands; advanced packaging becomes critical constraint
Korea's large chipmakers raiding fabless design talent; threatens mid-tier ASIC and AI accelerator design ecosystem
Taiwan fabless (Alchip model) scaling AI chips to mass production at advanced nodes, reinforcing regional design advantage

ko.counterpoint: Microsoft's ability to sustain 1M+ unit production volumes and compete on software stack integration vs. Nvidia remains unproven.

ko.executive_summary: TSMC revenue hits record highs for third consecutive month as AI demand surges; Microsoft pursuing 300,000 units for Maia 300 chip from TSMC, while Google and AWS race custom silicon roadmaps. Samsung exploring High-NA EUV for 1nm circa 2030; TSMC taking cautious approach to advanced nodes. TSMC-Sony joint venture announced for next-generation image sensors; SPIL ramping CoWoS advanced packaging to 2028 with NT$100B Yunlin investment.
key_facts: TSMC record revenue third consecutive month
Microsoft requesting 300,000 TSMC units for Maia 300
Samsung targeting High-NA EUV for 1nm around 2030
TSMC CoWoS 5.5-reticle yield >99%
TSMC-Sony joint venture for next-gen image sensors
SPIL Yunlin facility NT$100 billion investment; CoWoS online 2028
Memory and ABF materials identified as AI bottlenecks
Kioxia's largest shareholder now SK hynix-linked BCPE Pangea Cayman2

implications.text: Microsoft, Google, AWS, Nvidia all competing for TSMC allocation; record revenue reflects utilization peaks with memory/substrate supply constraints
Both TSMC and Samsung holding conservative stance on <2nm; cost, yield, and demand uncertainty tempering aggressive roadmap push
CoWoS yields strong but memory and ABF substrate supply identified as AI infrastructure constraints; SPIL expansion critical for 2028+
TSMC-Sony image sensor JV signals foundry expansion beyond compute; Kioxia ownership shift reflects industry consolidation and leverage plays

ko.counterpoint: TSMC revenue growth may moderate if hyperscaler custom chip timelines slip or macro demand weakens.
